caveats.devs_monthly_active: Electric Capital, week ending 2026-07-24. NOT comparable at face value: the figure rolls up each ecosystem's child ecosystems. Ethereum rolls up 1,391 children including every major L2; Cosmos Hub here is the HUB only (106), not the 1,408 IBC ecosystem; Kaspa has zero children so its 40 is first-party. Stellar's 3,937 jumped from ~1,320 in a year via repo additions to the taxonomy, not organic growth.
caveats.wallets_of_5: Native support only, out of MetaMask, Phantom, Trust, Exodus, Keplr. Community MetaMask Snaps and wrapped-token listings do not count.
caveats.custody: BitGo has Kaspa staged in its SDK (commits April and May 2026) but production returns 'Coin unsupported'. A KAS ticker exists at BitGo as an ERC20 on Ethereum, which is a false-positive trap. Copper lists Monero for external transfer only, not custody.
caveats.us_spot_etf: live means an 8-A12B plus EFFECT and an actual listing. filed means an S-1 on file and not effective.
caveats.steward: The entity presented on the chain's own pages. Kaspa and Monero name none; independent community non-profits exist for Kaspa but none is presented as the network's steward.
caveats.tps_sustained: Windows differ by what each chain publishes. Genuine 30-day means: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Litecoin, Monero, Sui, Aptos, Near, Kaspa. One-hour or one-day snapshots: Solana, BNB Chain, Cardano, Avalanche, TRON, TON, Hedera, Algorand, ICP, Stellar. Cardano's 0.14 is a quiet-hour reading and is not representative. Kaspa's 0.895 is a real 30-day mean but the chain is bursty: monthly means ran from 0.58 to 318.97 over the last year, and the peak hour hit 2,229.
caveats.tps_claimed: The project's own headline number where it publishes one. Sui's 200,000 is its docs figure for benchmark conditions, about 3,200 times the observed 62.79. Polkadot's 623,000 is extrapolated from a Kusama test at 23 percent of cores, not measured on Polkadot. Near's 1,000,000 and Aptos's 160,000 are second-hand from Chainspect, not fetched from the projects. Bitcoin, Litecoin, Monero, Kaspa, Near, Ethereum and Stellar publish no headline TPS.
caveats.nakamoto_coefficient: NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS ROWS. PoW chains here (Bitcoin 3, Litecoin 2, Monero 2, Kaspa 2) use one definition: pools controlling more than half of block production. PoS rows mostly use a 33-percent-of-stake threshold. Polkadot's 166 is the least trustworthy number in the set: a Polkadot Forum analysis puts it at 25, at 14 after clustering, and after finding one address cluster running 92 to 105 validators, at no more than 4. Polkadot is recorded as unknown here: the published figures span 166 to 4 depending on whether validators run by one operator are counted once or separately, and that is a disagreement rather than a measurement.
caveats.finality_s: PoW rows use 6 confirmations as the convention. Kaspa's 10 seconds is the practical settlement convention; its consensus finality boundary is 12 hours, or 432,000 blocks at 10 BPS. Cardano is probabilistic and its 120 seconds may be quoting the not-yet-live Peras target rather than live behavior, so it is recorded as unknown.
caveats.block_producers: Counts different things by design. PoW rows count mining pools seen producing blocks. Kaspa's 32 is distinct coinbase payout addresses over a 7-minute sample, so pools rotating addresses would inflate it. Hedera's 29 are permissioned council nodes; the public cannot run one.
caveats.smart_contracts: general means a full contract platform. limited means script-level rules only: Bitcoin Script, and for Kaspa post-Toccata, UTXO covenants plus ZK verifier precompiles, with no account-based VM.
caveats.daily_transactions: Counted on the most comparable basis available, with each chain's own headline shown alongside where the two differ. The headline is the inflated one every time. Kaspa's raw 737,701 is 89.5 percent coinbase; Solana's raw 281 million is 51.5 percent validator votes; Aptos's raw figure is 27.5 percent block metadata; TON counts one user action as several account-level transactions.
caveats.privacy_default: 2 means sender, receiver and amount are hidden by default. 0 means the ledger is public and anyone can read every payment. Only Monero is private by default here. Optional privacy tooling exists elsewhere but is not the default and is not counted.
caveats.devs_full_time: Electric Capital's full-time count: developers who committed code on 10 or more days in a month. The same ecosystem-rollup caveat as the monthly-active figure applies.
caveats.ethereum_classic_nakamoto: One coinbase address produced 62% of blocks over a 23-day sample, so the coefficient is 1. Consistent with ETC's history of 51% attacks.
caveats.pi_network: Smart contracts are on testnet only; the live mainnet shows no contract calls. Block producers and Nakamoto coefficient are unknown because Pi does not publish its quorum set, so whether the Core Team still controls block production cannot be verified.
caveats.stable_fees: Zero-fee is an opt-in sponsorship, not the default. Ordinary transfers pay a small fee.
caveats.tps_peak_observed: The highest rate each chain has actually been observed carrying. This is demonstrated capacity, not a claim and not a theoretical maximum. Read it beside the sustained figure: sustained is how much demand the chain gets, peak is how much it has proven it can take. Kaspa carries 0.9 and has demonstrated 2,229, which is a very different statement from 0.9 alone. Windows differ: Kaspa, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Litecoin and Monero are the highest full hour or day observed; the rest are Chainspect's highest across 100 consecutive blocks, which is a shorter and therefore flattering window.
caveats.filecoin_messages: Explorer message totals for Filecoin run roughly 20x the explicit on-chain message count, because they include internal and cron messages. The figure here is explicit messages only, and over half of those are storage proofs rather than user activity.
caveats.devs_rollup: Electric Capital ecosystem figures are recursive rollups of child ecosystems. Where a chain has no children the number is chain-alone; where it does, it is not. Kaspa has zero children.
caveats.scope: Twenty layer ones, chosen as the ones a reader is actually weighing Kaspa against. Dropped from an earlier set of 32: chains with almost no measurable public activity, or none an independent explorer can verify, where a ranking teaches nothing.
caveats.measurement: Ten of the twenty were re-measured against live endpoints on 1 Aug 2026. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Cardano and Stellar came from Blockchair's per-chain stats, taking block interval from blocks in 24h and demand from transactions in 24h. Avalanche, BNB Chain and Cronos came from their own RPC endpoints, timing 500 blocks; Solana from getBlockTime across 1000 slots. That work found real drift rather than rounding: Ethereum's sustained rate had been 34 percent high, Stellar's 53 percent, Cardano's 33 percent low. The remaining ten carry figures gathered earlier and not re-checked on that date, and each row records which of its fields were. Kaspa's 10 blocks per second is a protocol constant from the Crescendo fork, not a reading, so it is not in the measured list.

sources.devs: developerreport.com API and data.opendevdata.org parquet snapshot 20260731T125446
sources.sdks: each chain's own developer docs, official-vs-community distinction as that page draws it
sources.wallets: each wallet's own registry or supported-asset list: MetaMask support pages, Phantom help center, trustwallet/wallet-core registry.json, Exodus asset dataset, Keplr chain registry
sources.etf: SEC EDGAR 8-A12B and S-1 filings; CFTC CME reports for futures

Bitcoin.purpose: Money nobody can quietly change the rules on. The most settled asset in the category.
Bitcoin.weakness: Slow to settle and it barely programs. Three pools produce over half the blocks.

Ethereum.purpose: The default place to build a contract, and where most on-chain money sits.
Ethereum.weakness: Layer one is slow and dear; the cheap activity moved to rollups, which splits liquidity.

Solana.tx_note: 51.5% of the raw count is validator vote transactions
Solana.purpose: One fast chain for consumer apps, where everything shares the same state.
Solana.weakness: A 256 GB validator machine, and half its headline transaction count is validator votes.

BNB Chain.purpose: Cheap, fast, and wired into the largest exchange.
BNB Chain.weakness: 45 validators re-elected daily. Speed bought with a permissioned set.

Cardano.purpose: Formal methods and slow, deliberate change.
Cardano.weakness: Almost no measured throughput, and finality is probabilistic despite what trackers publish.

Avalanche.purpose: Sub-second finality with subnets for teams that want their own rules.
Avalanche.weakness: Real usage sits far below the 4,500 TPS it advertises.

TRON.purpose: The rail most dollar stablecoins actually move on.
TRON.weakness: 27 producers. Cheap and fast because very few parties run it.

Sui.tx_note: about 31% are system transactions, not user actions
Sui.purpose: Objects instead of accounts, so simple transfers skip consensus entirely.
Sui.weakness: Claims 200,000 TPS and carries 63. About half its transaction count is system overhead.

Aptos.tx_note: 27.5% of the raw count is block metadata and state checkpoints
Aptos.purpose: Move's safety guarantees with sub-second blocks.
Aptos.weakness: Publishes no finality figure at all, and 28% of its count is block metadata.

TON (Gram).tx_note: the raw count is account-level, so one user action becomes several
TON (Gram).purpose: Payments inside Telegram, at the scale of a messaging app.
TON (Gram).weakness: Counts one user action as several transactions, so its headline is roughly 6.5x inflated.

Near.purpose: Sharding that hides itself, and accounts that read like usernames.
Near.weakness: Genuine 8.5 TPS against a second-hand claim of a million.

Hedera.purpose: Enterprise governance: a named council of large companies runs the nodes.
Hedera.weakness: The public cannot run a consensus node. That is the design, not a gap.

Algorand.purpose: One-block finality and the smallest node in its class.
Algorand.weakness: Little measured activity, and a foundation that redomiciled to the US in 2026.

Litecoin.purpose: Bitcoin's design with faster blocks and near-zero fees.
Litecoin.weakness: Two pools produce 62% of blocks, and it runs far below its own demonstrated peak.

Monero.purpose: The only chain here where sender, receiver and amount are hidden by default.
Monero.weakness: No contracts, no custody at BitGo or Copper, no wallet support in the majors.

Kaspa.tx_note: 89.5% of the raw count is coinbase, one per block at 10 blocks per second
Kaspa.purpose: Proof of work that does not throw away the blocks that lose the race, with covenants on top.
Kaspa.weakness: 0.9 TPS measured, 40 developers, no custody, no ETF, and no major wallet.
Kaspa.sc_note: Covenants, covenant IDs and ZK proof checks, live since Toccata.

Polkadot.tx_note: not the relay chain, which carries almost no user transactions
Polkadot.purpose: Chains that share security instead of each buying their own.
Polkadot.weakness: The relay chain carries almost no user transactions, and its published Nakamoto coefficient ranges from 166 to 4 depending who counts.
Polkadot.sc_note: On Polkadot Hub, not the relay chain.

Internet Computer.purpose: Apps served straight from the chain, no cloud in front.
Internet Computer.weakness: 512 GB and 32 TB per node. Nobody runs this at home.

Stellar.purpose: Cross-border payments and asset issuance for institutions.
Stellar.weakness: Runs close to its own observed ceiling, and its developer count tripled through repo additions rather than growth.

Bitcoin Cash.purpose: Bitcoin's fork that kept bigger blocks and sub-cent fees.
Bitcoin Cash.weakness: 80% of its hashrate is unattributed, so nobody can say how concentrated mining is.
